tracking_policy: Record concrete creator decisions prospectively. Do not reconstruct earlier passes as if contemporaneously logged.

decisions.origin: creator direction
decisions.decision: Add a lightweight provenance layer to the canonical project workflow: a hash-chained stable-pass ledger, a central decision-to-implementation map, an honest authorship manifest, and a release fingerprint. Start from the current canonical GenVo8 state as a pre-provenance baseline and do not fabricate retrospective entries.
decisions.rationale: Preserve contemporaneous evidence of human design and technical direction in an AI-assisted workflow without keeping every historical ZIP or claiming AI-generated implementation as handwritten human code.

implementation.notes: The mutable tree-state file exists only to detect changed files between stable passes in a no-Git workflow. It is derived state, not authorship evidence by itself.

decisions.origin: creator direction
decisions.decision: Make v1.06 the first visible and mechanical lineage divergence pass. Convert the existing Independent Forager versus Colony Cohesion family behavior into inherited descendant forms beginning around Generation 2 or 3, so player-led family behavior visibly changes descendant bodies and creates different practical capabilities before expanding to additional lifestyle branches.
decisions.rationale: Playtesting repeatedly stalled at Generation 2 and evolution was not visually legible enough. The first divergence must prove that lived family choices can create a recognizably different creature rather than another hidden modifier, while keeping the default HUD simple and preserving the existing gene, adaptation, command, ecology, swimming, and provenance authorities.

implementation.notes: Behavioral tendency remains reversible family culture. Each descendant lineage form is assigned deterministically at birth and remains fixed on that individual. Forager forms emphasize travel and forage reach; Colony forms emphasize shelter storage and protection. Generation handoff and optional Population UI expose the result without restoring a permanent information wall.

decisions.origin: creator direction
decisions.decision: Make v1.07 directly address the Generation 2 stall by turning the first inherited Forager or Colony form into a lived G2 ecological challenge with a concrete population-scale unlock. Forager descendants prove their ranging form by opening an outer feeding route and can earn earlier Scout leadership. Colony descendants prove their social form by using family guidance to hold a kin gathering and can earn earlier satellite nesting. Keep this to one G2 progression layer before adding more lifestyle branches.
decisions.rationale: Playtesting repeatedly reached Generation 2 and then repeated founder chores. This pass needs to make G2 introduce a new purpose and begin shifting control toward species leadership without adding a conventional skill tree or cluttering the default HUD.

implementation.notes: Generation 2 now asks the lineage to express its inherited form in the world. Rangebreak rewards outer-range feeding with earlier Scout leadership. Kin Gathering rewards family-command coordination with earlier satellite nesting. Safety guidance still outranks these goals, and the permanent HUD remains compact.

decisions.origin: creator direction
decisions.decision: Continue the generation-progression work into Generation 3 by making the G2 leadership gains create a second population center instead of adding several new lifestyle branches. Forager G3 should establish an outer ranging band through family Scout guidance. Colony G3 should establish and occupy a real satellite home. The resulting center must affect autonomous family behavior so the lineage begins shifting from direct creature control toward population leadership.
decisions.rationale: The next planned problem after fixing the Generation 2 stall is the transition from intimate creature control toward species leadership and meaningful world expansion. A second persistent population center gives G3 a new purpose, makes family commands materially change the world, and creates concrete groundwork for later separated populations and speciation without introducing a conventional skill tree or multiplying branches before the first divergence loop is proven.

implementation.notes: G3 Forager leadership can establish a persistent Ranging Band after a relative holds a commanded Scout area. G3 Colony leadership must construct and occupy a real satellite shelter before it becomes a Satellite Colony. Matching autonomous inherited-form adults are split between the original family range and the new population center while Family Direction is Auto. Population centers are exposed only through optional views and territory overlay markers.

decisions.origin: creator direction
decisions.decision: Make the next post-G3 pass turn separated population centers into ecologically consequential places before adding full speciation. Local forage, competing species, predators, and family load should determine whether a Ranging Band or Satellite Colony is strong enough to support its population, and poor settlement choices should affect autonomous family behavior and future expansion rather than remaining equally useful markers.
decisions.rationale: The planned world-expansion layer requires stronger territory and resource competition, viable settlement placement, local carrying capacity, and competing species to affect where expansion is practical. Establishing these consequences now gives separated populations different lived pressures that can later drive genuine divergence without prematurely multiplying lifestyle branches or declaring new species.

implementation.notes: Population centers now derive STRONG, VIABLE, CONTESTED, or CRITICAL status and local carrying capacity from real nearby biomass, grazing history, competing feeders, predators, and family load. Pressured centers deterministically redirect part of their autonomous cohort toward stronger neighboring cells. G3 ranging and satellite settlement checks use the same viability layer. Default HUD remains unchanged; optional population and territory views expose the detail.

decisions.origin: creator direction
decisions.decision: Pause proto-speciation for one pass and use v1.10 to reduce first-run friction and make existing simulation depth legible during ordinary play. Guide the founder through food, water, pairing, home familiarity, and first shelter before full pressure returns; strengthen restrained age, illness, kinship, and Stalker-territory reads; and explain high-value adaptation, illness, shelter, and defense effects at the moment they actually change an outcome without restoring a permanent information wall.
decisions.rationale: Playtest feedback identified onboarding overload, weak at-a-glance population hierarchy, and a gap between deep simulation and immediate player understanding. Adding another evolutionary layer before players can readily perceive current causes and consequences would compound that problem. This pass prioritizes contextual explanation and visual hierarchy while preserving the existing simulation authorities and compact default HUD.

implementation.notes: The opening now remains protected through the first family shelter milestone. Effect feedback reads already-resolved simulation state and does not change adaptation math, ecology, illness, combat, or AI. Existing toast priority is respected so contextual explanations do not overwrite higher-priority interaction or ecology notices. Creature-state cues remain physical and restrained rather than becoming floating labels.

decisions.origin: creator direction
decisions.decision: After the v1.10 clarity pass, return to the evolutionary roadmap by recording separate lived ecological histories for the original Home Range and every established G3 population center. Track where lineage members are actually raised and which local pressures dominate, but do not turn those records into species changes yet. The purpose of v1.11 is to create prospective evidence that a later proto-speciation pass can consume without retroactive invention or a player-selected branch menu.
decisions.rationale: The existing G3 split and v1.09 center ecology already allow related populations to occupy different places, but the game did not yet remember those differences as population-specific history. Recording local scarcity, competitors, predators, crowding, moisture and thermal pressures now makes future divergence causally traceable to where descendants actually lived while preserving the rule that deeper evolution should emerge from behavior and environment use rather than a conventional skill tree.

implementation.notes: PopulationPressureMemoryController records eight read-only pressure axes per population plus per-animal residence days. Home and secondary centers accumulate independent histories. Secondary adult assignment and physical residence of young both contribute to population affinity. Optional Population/Home Range views and generation handoff can expose recorded history; the default HUD and all evolution authorities remain unchanged.

decisions.origin: creator direction
decisions.decision: Proceed from population-specific pressure memory into a restrained first proto-speciation pass. Sustained separation plus materially different recorded ecological pressures may produce one small inherited population trait in Generation 4 or later descendants, but the populations must remain one species for this pass. The inherited difference must arise from where the parental population actually lived and what it experienced, not from a branch-selection menu or a random evolution roll.
decisions.rationale: The project now has persistent secondary populations, local carrying pressure, and prospective population histories. Using those recorded histories to seed modest inherited differences is the next planned bridge toward eventual speciation, while keeping the causal chain visible and avoiding an abrupt jump from one species to several fully formed branches.

implementation.notes: A qualifying G4+ birth deterministically receives at most one proto-trait when the birth population has at least five recorded pressure days, population histories are sufficiently separated, a local pressure is materially stronger than comparison populations, and a parent has actually resided primarily in that population. Proto-traits provide modest physical and mechanical differences and preserve species='genvo'. Existing adaptation choice and lineage-form authorities remain separate.

decisions.origin: creator direction
decisions.decision: Continue the restrained proto-speciation path by proving that population traits behave like inheritance over several generations before declaring new species. A trait should reinforce under continued local pressure, persist but weaken after migration away from supporting pressure, and mix through reproduction between differently adapted populations. Gene flow must soften or redirect one dominant expressed proto-trait rather than stack multiple mechanical bonuses, and every descendant must remain GenVo8 in this pass.
decisions.rationale: v1.12 proved that separated populations can first express small pressure-derived differences, but a one-generation trait is not enough evidence for speciation. Persistence, dilution and gene flow are necessary to show whether ecological divergence can survive contact and whether geographic separation actually maintains distinct inherited tendencies over time.

implementation.notes: Proto traits now store origin population, lineage depth, inheritance state, gene-flow fraction and mixed ancestry. Continued qualified local pressure can reinforce a matching trait. Unsupported migration can carry a weaker expression into a new population. Cross-population reproduction keeps one locally expressed trait while recording and visually hinting at the other parent trait. No species ID or adaptation authority is changed.

decisions.origin: creator direction
decisions.decision: Proceed from multi-generation proto-trait inheritance into the first true speciation threshold, but require several generations of reinforced local divergence, sustained ecological separation, and low recent gene flow before recognizing a descendant species. Keep the young boundary reversible so renewed inter-population breeding or ecological convergence can push the population back below the threshold instead of making speciation a permanent scripted unlock.
decisions.rationale: v1.13 proved that local traits can persist, reinforce, weaken, and mix, so the game now has enough prospective evidence to distinguish maintained divergence from a temporary local adaptation. A demanding reversible threshold preserves the project rule that species emerge from lived behavior and ecology rather than a menu or arbitrary timer, while allowing gene flow to remain an active evolutionary force.

implementation.notes: A secondary population must satisfy independent history, ecology, physical separation, resident cohort, multi-generation trait, local-pressure, local-birth, and low-gene-flow gates for consecutive evaluations. Recognition creates a player-facing speciesBranch while preserving base species=genvo for existing simulation authorities. Sustained renewed gene flow or ecological convergence can collapse the young species boundary. The controller is deterministic and consumes no RNG.

decisions.origin: creator direction
decisions.decision: After proving a reversible species threshold, make recognized species useful as a persistent living evolutionary tree. Ancestral and descendant taxa should be able to coexist and be counted independently, rejoined or extinct branches must remain in lineage history instead of being erased, and later species formation must be able to branch from an already-recognized descendant species rather than always attaching directly to GenVo8.
decisions.rationale: v1.14 could recognize and later collapse a young species boundary, but collapse removed current branch identity from lineage records and the game had no durable taxonomic tree. Preserving historical branch formation while keeping current recognition reversible lets the player guide an actual branching evolutionary history and establishes the structural basis for independent extinction, coexistence, and second-order divergence.

implementation.notes: EvolutionaryTreeController stores a GenVo8 root plus durable descendant nodes with parentage, founding population, historical membership, and living/rejoined/extinct state. Lineage records retain speciesBranchHistory separately from current speciesBranch. Speciation recognition asks the tree for the dominant living parent taxon in the founding cohort and uses that parent population as the physical-separation reference for later branching. The Population panel exposes the tree; the default HUD and shared engine species registry remain unchanged.

decisions.origin: creator direction
decisions.decision: After establishing a living evolutionary tree, make multiple living taxa matter operationally. Family guidance should default to the active taxon, mating should expose cross-branch gene flow, and successor control should prefer the current taxon while preserving an explicit player choice to lead another living branch.
decisions.rationale: v1.15 made species branches durable and visible but ordinary commands, mate selection, and control handoff still behaved as if the lineage were one undifferentiated family. Scoping those interactions to the active taxon turns the evolutionary tree into gameplay while preserving direct creature control and deliberate gene flow.

implementation.notes: When multiple taxa coexist, broad and radial guidance default to the active taxon and can be explicitly toggled to whole-lineage scope. Local marks preserve the scope they were placed with. Mate discovery prioritizes same-taxon candidates but keeps cross-taxon gene flow possible and visible. Successor choice prefers the active taxon while deliberate cross-branch handoff remains available and is recorded in generation presentation. No species threshold, stat bonus, or RNG authority is added.

decisions.origin: creator direction
decisions.decision: After making living species branches controllable, make coexistence matter in the shared world. Different taxa should consume and compete within the same real local ecology, receive branch-specific relief or expansion goals when their origin ranges are stressed, prefer same-taxon autonomous mating while retaining gene flow, and be able to establish taxon-scoped settlements that other branches do not automatically share.
decisions.rationale: v1.16 made commands, mate choice, and leadership branch-aware, but species could still coexist without materially changing carrying quality or settlement behavior. Feeding cross-taxon overlap back into the existing population ecology and shelter authorities makes species leadership consequential without inventing an abstract strategy meter or parallel resource system.

implementation.notes: SpeciesCoexistenceController reads the living evolutionary tree, existing population centers, residence history, local biomass, predators, carrying state, and physical cross-taxon overlap. Cross-taxon lineage members count as real competitors in branch-owned population ecology. Dynamic taxon goals use the existing Task Guide. Autonomous adults can redistribute under branch pressure without overriding survival or explicit commands. Autonomous mating prefers the same living taxon before gene-flow fallback. Taxon-scoped Nest projects require matching workers, create branch-owned shelters, and register species-settlement population centers. No new resource, species threshold, hidden stat bonus, or RNG authority is introduced.

decisions.origin: creator direction
decisions.decision: After proving population divergence, speciation, a persistent evolutionary tree, and species-level coexistence, return to the broader lifestyle-evolution roadmap. Start with a restrained four-lifestyle proof set: aquatic, nomadic, guardian, and burrower. Each lifestyle must emerge from sustained taxon behavior, habitat use, already-earned traits, and population pressure rather than from a skill-tree menu, and each must open or strengthen a genuinely different way of living in the existing world.
decisions.rationale: The evolutionary infrastructure is mature enough that new ecological niches can now belong to individual living taxa instead of becoming universal upgrades. Limiting this pass to four lifestyles tests whether species branches can acquire recognizable lifestyles with real movement, shelter, defense, and habitat consequences before expanding into hunter, grazer, climbing, gliding, or other niche branches.

implementation.notes: SpeciesLifestyleController consumes existing movement history, population pressure memory, taxon residence, lineage form, adaptations, shelter use, and the evolutionary tree. A G4+ taxon needs at least two adults, three pressure-memory days, and three consecutive qualifying days before one lifestyle establishes. Aquatic changes swimming and dry-land efficiency; Nomadic changes travel/search range and open-range preference; Guardian changes threat sensing and sheltered defense; Burrower changes nest material cost, shelter protection/thermal insulation, open movement, and denning preference. Lifestyle state is taxon-level, deterministic, consumes no RNG, and remains separate from adaptations, proto-traits, and speciation. Hunter and grazer lifestyle branches are intentionally deferred.

decisions.origin: creator direction
decisions.decision: Treat the reported lag during movement and actions as a release-blocking responsiveness problem before adding more lifestyle content. Optimize worst-frame latency rather than relying on average render time, while preserving the v1.18 simulation rules and visible game behavior.
decisions.rationale: Live playtesting exposed input and movement hitches that the existing mean-render benchmark did not reveal. Instrumentation found synchronous daily terrain invalidation causing roughly 300-400 ms stalls, movement-time terrain cache misses, repeated lifestyle resolution in the 64 Hz control path, first-input audio work, and avoidable daily vegetation/dispersal overhead. The hotfix must remove those main-thread spikes without changing progression, ecology formulas, or species/lifestyle design.

implementation.notes: Renderer terrain uses stale-while-refresh 4x4 chunks, delayed daily habitat-field refresh, offscreen prewarming, and throttled background rebuilds instead of daily synchronous cache invalidation. Player prediction includes the same divergence/proto/lifestyle speed modifiers as authority. Established lifestyles fast-return from creature cache. Audio bulk initialization is deferred/paced around input and movement keydown no longer creates the audio context. Vegetation reuses per-day plant descriptors and dispersal caches plant hashes/directions. No simulation RNG source, progression threshold, lifestyle rule, or ecology formula is intentionally changed.

decisions.origin: creator direction
decisions.decision: After confirming the v1.18.1 responsiveness hotfix restored smooth play, deepen the four existing species lifestyles into distinct day-to-day gameplay loops before adding more lifestyle branches. Aquatic taxa should actually use water as ordinary habitat and colonization space, Nomadic taxa should behave as moving populations through the existing migration system, Guardian taxa should hold and intercept around threatened kin and shelters, and Burrower taxa should create visibly distinct dens and return to them under strain or weather.
decisions.rationale: v1.18 proved that lifestyles could emerge at the taxon level, but their player-facing consequences were still too close to passive bonuses. Making each established lifestyle alter autonomous behavior, habitat use, settlement structure, and contextual goals lets the player feel the branch identity in ordinary play. Preserving the confirmed-smooth v1.18.1 frame-time behavior is a hard release constraint.

implementation.notes: No new lifestyle type, combat authority, migration authority, shelter authority, species threshold, or RNG source is introduced. Aquatic extends canonical swimming and wet-range guidance; Nomadic adjusts thresholds inside the existing MigrationController; Guardian uses canonical guard/mob intents around real threats; Burrower modifies canonical shelters into den-style structures and uses existing shelter-return behavior. The v1.18.1 worst-frame performance contracts remain part of the release gate.

decisions.origin: creator direction
decisions.decision: Treat the dense, clipped Population, Home Range, and Help panels plus the finicky fourth-child Stalker lesson as usability defects before further feature expansion. Keep all underlying simulation data, but present it summary-first with reachable detail, and make fleeing from a real Stalker encounter an explicit valid survival lesson for young.
decisions.rationale: Live playtesting showed that deep simulation data was technically available but difficult to read, with lower content cut off, while the Danger lesson required awkward child/Stalker positioning and failed to recognize a sensible player flee response. The correction should improve legibility and teach the intended survival behavior without removing diagnostic depth or changing predator balance.

implementation.notes: Population and Home Range use compact summaries plus expandable internally scrollable sections; Help is topic-grouped. Live panel refresh preserves scroll and details-open state. The Danger lesson widens observation beyond bite-danger distance, temporarily tightens juvenile follow only while Danger is next, and accepts movement away from an engaged/pursuing Stalker as a flee response. No Stalker damage/pursuit authority, global family AI, evolution authority, or simulation RNG source is changed. The v1.18.1 worst-frame performance contract remains a release gate.

decisions.origin: creator direction
decisions.decision: After a G2 descendant finds and pairs with a distant mate, allow that pair to establish a second brood shelter before population-scale satellite nesting unlocks, and make the birth-preparation task guide the pair into using that new home instead of forcing a return to the founder shelter.
decisions.rationale: Live playtesting showed that the one-shelter direct-build rule made G2 feel artificially anchored to the founder home precisely when distant mate-finding should create a natural reason to found a new household. The early second shelter should be a real ShelterController structure with ordinary material, terrain, and family-use rules, while larger multi-home expansion remains governed by the existing satellite-nesting progression.

implementation.notes: A paired G2+ active descendant can directly establish one brood shelter for that pair before satellite-nest population thresholds, provided the site is dry, supplied, and separated from an existing usable family shelter. Early family shelter capacity becomes two for an eligible paired G2+ descendant. The pregnancy/birth-preparation task prefers and stocks the new brood shelter. A pair cannot use this route to spam repeated direct shelters; population-scale expansion still belongs to the existing nesting authority.

decisions.origin: creator direction
decisions.decision: Make autonomous GenVo8 creatures visually walk continuously between simulation states instead of appearing to hop from square to square. Keep authoritative movement speed and AI decisions unchanged, but use constant visual travel between ecology ticks and keep the gait active while the rendered body is still crossing that segment.
decisions.rationale: Live playtesting showed a large presentation-quality gap: the controlled creature used smooth live movement while relatives and wildlife visibly eased to a stop and restarted on each 8 Hz simulation step. Technically interpolated movement still read as grid hopping. The correction belongs in presentation, not in AI speed or simulation cadence, and must preserve the confirmed smooth-play performance baseline.

implementation.notes: Autonomous visual motion now uses linear interpolation between authoritative poses and exposes in-segment travel state so gait animation remains active until the visual segment completes. Simulation coordinates, 8 Hz ecology timing, path decisions, movement speed, and RNG are unchanged. The v1.18.1 worst-frame latency contract remains a release gate.

decisions.origin: creator direction
decisions.decision: Close the remaining animation-quality gap between the controlled GenVo and autonomous creatures. Keep AI movement authority unchanged, but make autonomous limb/body gait advance from actual rendered travel, preserve moving presentation across tiny ecology-step seams, orient bodies to their visual travel heading, and keep lifted GenVo legs visibly articulated instead of blinking out at the top of a step.
decisions.rationale: Live playtesting found that after v1.21 fixed square-to-square position hopping, only the player-controlled creature still looked convincingly animated while walking. The remaining defect was presentation cadence and limb articulation, not simulation movement. The correction belongs in the renderer/motion bridge and must preserve the confirmed smooth-play performance baseline.

implementation.notes: VisualMotionTracker accumulates presentation-only gait phase from interpolated travel distance and exposes recent movement/heading without mutating animal state. Autonomous renderers use that gait phase and travel heading; species-specific sprite code remains authoritative for walk/hop/prowl style. GenVo raised feet fold inward and retain lower-leg/toe rendering through high-step frames. Simulation positions, AI decisions, pathing, collisions, speeds, energy costs, RNG, saves, and ecology cadence are unchanged. The v1.18.1 worst-frame latency contract remains a release gate.

decisions.origin: creator direction
decisions.decision: Improve species-specific autonomous body animation after the v1.22 coordinate and gait smoothing pass. Keep locomotion authority unchanged, but make Hoppers visibly launch/tuck/replant, Diggers undulate and alternate working claws, and Stalkers prowl with diagonal planted/recovery legs, shoulder/head counter-motion, and tail balance so wildlife no longer reads as rigid sprites sliding through the world.
decisions.rationale: Live play showed that smooth coordinates alone were not enough: non-player fauna still looked less alive than the controlled GenVo. The next pass should improve physical animation language without raising simulation cadence or risking the responsiveness regression already fixed in v1.18.1.

implementation.notes: All new gait values are deterministic presentation outputs derived from the existing fractional rendered-travel phase. No AI, movement speed, pathing, combat, collision, ecology, RNG, or save authority changes.

decisions.origin: creator direction
decisions.decision: Set up the GenVo8 itch.io page as a real public-facing game page now that the v1.23 simulation has a stable identity: lead with the lineage fantasy, use accurate discovery metadata and AI disclosure, present a restrained field/river visual theme, and show real v1.23 runtime screenshots rather than mockups.
decisions.rationale: The existing live itch page is effectively a bare play link with little player-facing explanation. The page should explain what the player actually does and why the multigeneration ecosystem is distinctive without turning the store description into a changelog or technical manual.

implementation.notes: Store-page preparation only. No gameplay/runtime authority changed; the public v1.23.0 build remains the same release payload.

decisions.origin: creator direction
decisions.decision: Add real save/load support now that live players are refreshing the browser and losing their lineage. Persist the living GenVo8 simulation, not just the active creature, provide Continue and New lineage at startup, autosave without reintroducing the v1.18.1 action/movement hitch, and keep a versioned save schema for future migration.
decisions.rationale: A multigeneration lineage game asks players to invest in descendants, shelters, population splits, species branches, and ecosystem history. Losing all of that on refresh breaks the central promise of the game. Persistence must therefore cover the canonical simulation authorities and must be scheduled away from the control/render hot path.

implementation.notes: IndexedDB schema 1 stores a structured-clone snapshot of mutable world state, animals, RNG, and controller-owned state. Restore instantiates normal authorities without bootstrap spawning, rebinds controller simulation references, restores mutable arrays, and rebuilds derived spatial buckets. Autosave is debounced/idle-scheduled with milestone and visibility triggers; manual save/load and startup Continue/New lineage are also exposed. Browser/device-local persistence only.

decisions.origin: creator direction
decisions.decision: Expand GenVo8 after save/load by adding Hunter and Grazer as emergent diet lifestyles. They must come from repeated lived feeding behavior and inherited biological support, change autonomous behavior and population resource pressure, remain compatible with existing saves, and preserve the v1.18.1 smooth-play baseline.
decisions.rationale: The existing four lifestyles proved that taxon-scale ways of life can emerge from play. The next expansion should make food-web position diverge too, so a lineage can become an active predator or a plant specialist through what it repeatedly does rather than through another menu unlock.

implementation.notes: Hunter and Grazer use prospective daily diet evidence and the existing three-day lifestyle establishment rule. Hunter gains autonomous live-prey pursuit, prey-based carrying pressure, and a plant tradeoff. Grazer gains earlier plant foraging, plant-energy efficiency, and animal-food tradeoffs. Existing persistence captures the new controller fields generically, with missing daily counters normalized for v1.24 saves.

decisions.origin: AI-assisted implementation choice following creator instruction to proceed with expansion
decisions.decision: Deepen the newly established Hunter and Grazer lifestyles with food-web feedback before adding more lifestyle labels. Hunter GenVo8 should become visible ecological danger to edible wildlife, while Grazer lineages should respond to the real grazing history they create by rotating toward fresher feeding ground.
decisions.rationale: v1.25 made diet specialization mechanically real for the lineage itself, but the surrounding ecosystem did not fully react. The next expansion should make those choices produce readable consequences in prey behavior and landscape use without creating a second predator, alarm, plant, or migration authority.

implementation.notes: Simulation.isPredatorTo is shared by ordinary prey threat decisions and social alarm propagation. Grazer target ranking reuses existing grazing/recovery history and bounded local sampling. No new RNG or save schema is introduced; Stalker-only combat/territory authorities remain Stalker-only.

decisions.origin: creator direction from live playtest feedback
decisions.decision: Keep one-creature-at-a-time embodiment but make family agency explicit: Tab switches temporary control among living founder-line relatives, a visible AUTO quick-menu toggle lets the selected creature resume autonomous behavior, direct input immediately retakes control, and expandable data rows must use larger click targets.
decisions.rationale: Live feedback showed that players could not see how much the simulation had expanded and found idle stretches unplayable. The creator approved family switching and menu-driven automation as optional agency without turning unrelated wildlife into player units, and separately identified the tiny expandable-data controls as difficult to locate and click.

implementation.notes: Temporary Tab control changes playerId/player flag only. LineageTracker.activeId changes only through explicit succession. AUTO routes the selected creature through autonomous decision authorities and is cancelled by direct movement or world actions. Disclosure rows use the whole summary row as a minimum 36 px target with a 22 px visible marker. Save schema 1 remains compatible.

decisions.origin: creator direction for v1.28 Decisions Under Pressure
decisions.decision: Make Stalker encounters a decision between fleeing, hiding, fighting and bracing: add short-term exertion (breath) spent by sprint, brace and attack with quick recovery and no fatigue collapse; remove attack from E and add a dedicated attack key with wind-up and recovery; add a held Brace that protects only toward the attacker, slows movement, costs breath and cannot be held forever; run engaged Stalker pursuit in real time at a speed between walk and sprint, with pursuit stamina, giving up when tired or when line of sight breaks; make dense cover meaningful for every GenVo8.
decisions.rationale: Engaged Stalkers moved on the ambient life stride, so walking away always escaped, and E's priority list made sprinting in and mashing E the dominant answer. The creator asked for real choices under pressure, with an accepted runtime recording where flee, fight and brace each succeed in different circumstances and Shift+E fails. The broad-goals tutorial rewrite was split into its own pass after controls are final.

implementation.notes: Space attacks, hold J braces. Save schema 2 with in-place migration from schema 1. Engaged pursuit uses the local spatial query only while a hunt exists or may have started.

decisions.origin: creator direction for v1.28 (tutorial as broad goals instead of chores)
decisions.decision: Replace the fixed six-step opening lesson with three broad goals shown together and completable in any order (stay fed and watered, find a mate, make a home), with one suggested next step chosen from current needs and contextual key prompts instead of keys taught up front.
decisions.rationale: The roadmap lists tutorial as broad goals instead of chores for v1.28, and the design review recommends surfacing verbs near the creature when relevant. Split into its own pass after controls were final.

implementation.notes: Legacy saved stages move, food, drink, mate, home and shelter resume as goals. Safe start ends when all goals are done or the first shelter is built.

decisions.origin: creator roadmap v1.29 Observer Play
decisions.decision: Add 1x / 2x / 4x time controls tied to AUTO: speeding up hands the selected creature to its own AI, manual input returns to 1x, danger to the creature or family slows back to 1x automatically, and each return to 1x reports a short event summary. Verify 4x performance with large populations.
decisions.rationale: Testers said nothing happens while the simulation runs underneath. Observer play lets the player watch outcomes faster without missing decisions that need them.

implementation.notes: Speed is runtime-only and not saved. The simulation advances through the same control steps and ecology ticks; only the number per real second changes.

decisions.origin: creator roadmap v1.30 Habits
decisions.decision: Player actions train habits in the controlled creature, offspring weakly imitate caregivers, autonomous AI reads habits, the teaching checklist folds into learned behavior, creature cards show short habit summaries, and family tendencies aggregate from real creature habits.
decisions.rationale: The design review found that how you play did not change what your young become. Habits make behavior persist through creatures instead of a fixed curriculum, built through cognition, family observation, autonomous decisions and the tendency controller rather than on top of them.

implementation.notes: Habits are not genetic. Save schema 3 with in-place migration from schemas 1 and 2. Lesson tracking still drives independence and practice readiness.

decisions.origin: creator roadmap v1.31 Succession as Selection
decisions.decision: Variation appears in actual offspring, inherited body differences become more visible, handoff chooses among living descendants, mate choice matters more, the adaptation draft begins retirement, and existing adaptation saves migrate rather than disappear.
decisions.rationale: The design review called the pick-one-of-three handoff draft the skill tree GenVo8 should not be. Selection among real, varied descendants keeps evolution coming from lived conditions.

implementation.notes: Founder-line heredity only; wild inheritance unchanged. Draft kept behind CFG.evolution.handoffDraft for pending saves. Save schema 4.

decisions.origin: creator approval of consolidation Stage B
decisions.decision: Unify lived pressure into one vocabulary (scarcity, competition, predation, crowding, dryness, wetness, heat, cold, disease, few mates) shared by per-creature exposure, population memory, proto-traits, species evidence and adaptation emergence.
decisions.rationale: The consolidation plan found two pressure vocabularies describing the same lived conditions. One vocabulary is the first step toward fewer canonical values without adding a layer.

implementation.notes: Save schema 5 renames legacy kinds. Webbed Limbs emergence now reads wetness. Stage A baseline unchanged.

decisions.origin: creator direction to proceed with the consolidation plan
decisions.decision: Route every lineage-driven travel, forage range, threat sense, shelter exposure, metabolism and water-use effect through one function per effect with a shared limit, so stacks are bounded and single systems keep their full effect.
decisions.rationale: The Stage A baseline showed stacked range at 3.2 times neutral and stacked travel near sprint speed. One pipeline removes the scattered multiplication chains without adding a layer.

implementation.notes: Baseline regenerated deliberately: only the three stack rows changed. Save schema unchanged at 5.

decisions.origin: creator direction: adaptations become thresholds of anatomy and genes; keep heir choice
decisions.decision: Replace discrete inherited adaptation objects with twelve inherited anatomy values; adaptations are expressed at thresholds (tier 2 is the same body part developed further), lived pressure grows the matching body part in newborns over generations, and successor and journal cards show parts close to a threshold.
decisions.rationale: James's continuation order said v1.31 still treated adaptations as discrete objects rather than expressions of anatomy and genes, and that consolidation should fix that without losing heir choice.

implementation.notes: Adaptation list is a cache of expressed anatomy. Save schema 6 converts adaptations to anatomy with no gain or loss. Stage A baseline unchanged.

decisions.origin: creator direction: continue consolidation with Stage E (forms and proto-traits become anatomy readings)
decisions.decision: Store lineage form strength (reach or compact frame) and proto-trait strength (one body axis per trait) on inherited anatomy; the form and trait labels are read from whichever axis is developed. lineageForm and populationTrait remain as a cache of that reading plus its history until Stage G.
decisions.rationale: The v1.32 consolidation plan treats forms and proto-traits as labels for bodies rather than separate stored objects, so later stages (lifestyle readings) can read one body.

implementation.notes: Directly edited caches fold back into anatomy. Save schema 7 moves every form and proto-trait onto the body with no gain or loss. Stage A baseline unchanged, including natural AUTO runs.

decisions.origin: creator direction: proceed with Stage F using the default (a lifestyle stays once it forms; the body and habit reading decides when it forms)
decisions.decision: Recognize taxon lifestyles from the adults' average anatomy (including form and proto-trait axes), expressed adaptations, settled habits, lived population pressure and residence, with no lifestyle score of its own; daily travel, meal and hunt counts only drive the play loops of an established lifestyle, which stays once formed. Fold the G2 trials into any-order goals read from state (one lived event plus the habit the inherited form implies) and show G3 population goals as the same checklist. Strategy branch remains a reading of adaptations.
decisions.rationale: The v1.32 consolidation plan treats lifestyles and specialization as readings of body, adaptations and habits, and asks that scripted generation trials follow the v1.28 opening-goals pattern.

implementation.notes: Hunter now forms from a settled hunting habit plus a hunting build; Grazer from Efficient Gut, Forager form and no hunting habit; Burrower from a home habit instead of where adults stood that day. Rangebreak needs a ranging habit and Kin Gathering a home habit in addition to their events. Save schema stays 7; trial fields added at runtime default safely. Stage A baseline unchanged.

decisions.origin: creator direction: queue the terrain fix (stale landform masks after the title-screen world is swapped for a loaded or new world)
decisions.decision: When the renderer's world changes, clear every cache keyed only by tile position (landform masks, habitat masks, land and water base tiles, static land tiles, terrain chunks and refresh queue) and rebuild the habitat field for the new world.
decisions.rationale: The swap cleared terrain chunks but kept per-tile masks from the title world, so title-world land drew as flat land with a stepped bank over loaded-world water, and the reverse showed phantom water.

implementation.notes: Reproduced in Chromium by loading a save from a different world through loadSavedLineage; the same lakeside view is correct after the fix. No simulation or save change.

decisions.origin: creator report: the drink quest is no longer registering properly
decisions.decision: Show each half of the opening 'Fed and watered' goal as soon as it is done, and read opening firsts (first drink, first meal) from cognition's permanent seen record instead of only the 24-entry recent history.
decisions.rationale: Drinking was recorded, but the combined goal stayed unticked until the creature also ate, so a drink looked unregistered; and once more than 24 later events were logged the first drink scrolled out of history and the goal could never tick again, because a first is recorded only once.

implementation.notes: Reproduced in Chromium on v1.32.3 with a real E press at a bank. No simulation or save change.

decisions.origin: creator direction: proceed with consolidation Stage G cleanup
decisions.decision: Remove the Stage E lineageForm and populationTrait caches and their fold-back sync: form and proto-trait strength live only on anatomy, history on formHistory and protoHistory, and every reader in the game, tests and tools uses the readings. Save schema 8 converts older caches. Remove dead Stage F lifestyle evidence code. Record the consolidated model in the simulation spec. The adaptation list stays as the expression cache that ability checks read, and per-system effect factors stay as the inputs the Stage C pipeline combines.
decisions.rationale: The v1.32 plan's final stage removes old fields once two passes have matched; Stages E and F matched the baseline exactly.

implementation.notes: Stage A baseline unchanged including natural runs. Readings are pure and never mutate the animal.

decisions.origin: creator direction: knowledge inheritance and loss, with the successor knowing only what it learned itself
decisions.decision: Water banks and shelters become places a particular lineage creature knows (cognition), alongside its forage patches (foraging). A place is learned by using it or by being shown it by a caregiver during the existing family lessons; a taught copy is less sure, can be a little off, and does not carry how picked-over a patch was. Places grow less sure when not revisited and are forgotten after 16 days. What only one creature knew dies with it and leaves a field note. After the founder's opening, a thirsty creature is guided only to water it knows, or told to search.
decisions.rationale: Roadmap item 4 after the v1.32 consolidation: knowledge should be held by individuals, taught imperfectly, forgotten and lost, through existing systems and with no visible meters.

implementation.notes: Teaching consumes no RNG. Autonomous navigation to water is unchanged. Save schema stays 8. Stage A baseline unchanged.

decisions.origin: creator direction: one evolved active ability end to end (Pounce), targeting only a creature in front, player-controlled only
decisions.decision: Add Pounce as the first body ability: available when the rear-leg tendons (the Spring Tendons body part) are developed past 0.8, not an adaptation. Shift+Space toward a Stalker or prey in front within 2.5 to 3.5 tiles starts a still crouch, a leap that stops at water or rock, the normal bite on landing (a stronger hit on a Stalker, a better chance on prey) and a longer recovery, longest after a miss. It costs 32 breath; without the body, the breath or a target in front, Shift+Space is the ordinary bite. Lineages already expressing Spring Tendons keep developing the part under predator, scarcity or dryness pressure, and successor cards show Close to: Pounce.
decisions.rationale: Roadmap item 5: one evolved active ability built on anatomy thresholds and the existing attack, breath and wind-up systems with no new meter.

implementation.notes: No RNG added to heredity; Stage A baseline unchanged. Autonomous creatures do not pounce.

decisions.origin: creator direction: proceed with ecological consequences, starting with learned fear (grazing scars held for explicit approval)
decisions.decision: Where a Stalker attacks or kills a lineage creature becomes a danger place in the knowledge system: the surviving victim and relatives within 8 tiles learn it, young are taught it by a caregiver wary near it, it lasts 24 days, steers autonomous family's optional trips (feeding, exploring, roaming, migrating) out of a 4-tile zone while sureness is 0.25 or more, removes feared feeding grounds from route suggestions, speaks up when the active creature walks back into it, and dies with those who hold it. Also fixes a double stagger that kept self-learned shelters from being recorded in live play since v1.33.0.
decisions.rationale: Roadmap item 6: an ecological consequence that builds on the knowledge, habits and Stalker systems; families can carry an avoidance of a place after the danger has gone until it fades or the last holder dies.

implementation.notes: No RNG consumed. Survival needs (drinking when parched, escape, mobbing) are never overridden, nor is the player's control. Stage A baseline unchanged: Stalkers target abundant prey, so fear arises mostly from encounters with the active creature.

decisions.origin: creator approval: build grazing scars and regenerate the baseline on purpose
decisions.decision: Ground whose grazing wear exceeds 0.6 (roughly the most-worked 1% of grazed tiles) regrows more slowly, losing up to 40% of normal regrowth at wear 1.6 or more. The scar only slows regrowth, never removes plants, and heals as grazing wear decays (about 4.5% a day). An earlier tuning (wear 0.35, up to 55%) scarred ordinary grazing and collapsed Diggers in the 20-year ecology test, so it was rejected.
decisions.rationale: Roadmap item 6: overgrazing should have a lasting local consequence that pushes families and herds to move on, using the grazing history the game already recorded but never fed back.

implementation.notes: Stage A baseline regenerated on purpose: factor matrix identical; natural runs EVO-A deaths 29 to 24, EVO-C 23 to 20, family forage range medians 10.35 to 10.40 and 8.09 to 8.11; EVO-B unchanged. The 20-year ecology stability test, failing since v1.27 (Hoppers 15 of 16), now passes.

decisions.origin: creator direction: runtime/UI/playtest pass making observer play, AUTO relatives, habits, successor comparison and body variation understandable; first slice
decisions.decision: Successor cards draw each descendant's body portrait (genes, adaptations, inherited form and proto-trait). In AUTO the HUD line under the creature says what it is doing now (including when fear is steering it). The journal's Places remembered lists what the creature itself knows (water banks, food patches, shelters) and the places it fears, replacing the old last-glimpse lines and their broken 'today ago' wording.
decisions.rationale: A UI playtest tour showed body variation was only described in words on the successor cards, AUTO gave no sign of what the creature was doing, and the journal still showed pre-knowledge memory slots.

implementation.notes: Presentation only; no simulation change. Stage A baseline unchanged.

decisions.origin: creator direction: proceed with the next readability slices in order (habits on TAB, what changed at handoff, clearer AUTO relatives)
decisions.decision: Switching to a relative with TAB names it with its settled habits and what it knows and fears; the HUD habit line wraps to two lines instead of cutting off. The handoff reveal's visible lead says what the new creature brings (habits, known places, fears). Relatives on screen near you carry a small marker: a gold pip while carrying out your Family Command, a faint hollow ring while acting on their own.
decisions.rationale: Readability pass slices 2 to 4: habits, inheritance beyond the body, and who is following you were not visible without opening panels.

implementation.notes: Presentation only. Stage A baseline unchanged.

decisions.origin: creator direction: continue the readability pass with the next highest-value slice after touring the real screens
decisions.decision: In AUTO the opening goals describe what the creature is doing on its own and say plainly that a home needs you (AUTO never builds a home; take over and press N), and any goal that names a key adds that you have to take over to do it.
decisions.rationale: A natural AUTO tour showed the opening goals giving manual key instructions for 48 in-game days while the home goal could never complete without the player.

implementation.notes: Presentation only. Whether AUTO founders should build a first home is a gameplay change left for the creator to decide.

decisions.origin: creator decision (decision card, relayed by the coordinator): yes, AUTO should build a first home
decisions.decision: While AUTO is on, the active creature builds the family's first shelter on its own once its home range settles and the ordinary build conditions hold (the same canBuildHere and constructOrRepair path as N), checked once a second. The Stalker opening grace then ends exactly as it does when the player builds. Second homes and brood shelters remain the player's choice. The AUTO opening-goal text now says it will build on its own.
decisions.rationale: Observer play could never get past the opening: AUTO never built a shelter, so the Home goal never completed and the grace period never ended.

implementation.notes: Stage A baseline regenerated on purpose because its natural runs use AUTO: factor matrix identical; deaths EVO-A 24 to 22, EVO-B 15 to 19; family forage range medians EVO-A 10.40 to 10.78, EVO-B 8.38 to 8.30, EVO-C 8.11 to 10.09; one Grasping Limbs no longer appears in EVO-C by day 60. Homes are built on day 4 to 6 in headless AUTO runs.

decisions.origin: creator decision: adopt GenVo8 Evolution Expansion GDD v1 (section 0 locked creative decisions), salvage the paused v1.34.0 Shape and spring work, and start Phase A
decisions.decision: Follow the GDD: guided evolution, a lineage-level editor only at a valid reproductive handoff with no edits to living creatures, a mutation budget of base 8 MP plus a capped earned bonus of 0 to 4, a part graph and one phenotype resolver that adapts the existing authorities, delivered in Phases A to H. Salvage: the v1.34.0 activity ledger becomes the earned-bonus input (lineage/evolution-budget.js); the newborn shaping nudge, all spending on living creatures, the points HUD chip and toasts are removed; the development-drawn body code is kept as a Phase B note and the v1.33.7 sprite is restored exactly. Phase A (EV-001 to EV-005): frozen v1.33.7 baseline, PartRegistry v0 with the 18 starter parts, BodyPlan graph with validation, serialization and canonical ids, the legacy anatomy read adapter, and the phenotype resolver adapter.
decisions.rationale: Playtesters asked for deeper, more Spore-like evolution; the creator's GDD sets the design and requires a no-op contract foundation before anything visible changes.

implementation.notes: Phase A gate met: all 113 frozen v1.33.7 creatures migrate to valid plans and resolve to identical adaptations, adaptation effects, Pounce reach and availability, carrying and water results; the Stage A baseline, including same-seed natural runs, is byte-identical to v1.33.7; the 20-year ecology test passes. Nothing visible changes; plans are not yet stored in saves (anatomy stays the authority until a later phase moves one with its own tests and save transform).

decisions.origin: creator decision: build the starter parts as pixel components drawn in code in the current GenVo8 style (no external art), then Phase B
decisions.decision: Phase B (EV-006, EV-007): every starter part gets a procedural pixel component with layer and 8-facing / 8-frame metadata; a creature assembler turns a body plan (an explicit animal.bodyPlan, or the legacy adapter from expressed adaptations) into a cached per-socket layout; the GenVo8 sprite draws legs, spurs, mouth, eyes, flanks, dorsal, tail and torso from that layout. Parts that existed in v1.33.7 reuse its exact pixels; the only change to existing creatures is a heel tendon on Spring Tendons legs. New parts (spade, claw, venom gland, wide-field eye, reinforced ridge, paddle tail) were drawn bolder after a first capture showed them too faint.
decisions.rationale: GDD Phase B: visible assembly in eight facings with connected limbs in motion and attack, within the v1.18.1 performance floor, before the editor.

implementation.notes: Gate met: in-browser captures of a body using every new part in eight facings, walking and pouncing show it connected; a recorded-pixel comparison of all 113 fixture creatures over 8 facings, 8 frames, still and walking is identical to v1.35.0 apart from the spring heel; 560-animal observer probe 16.7 ms median and p95 at 1x to 4x; decision probe 5/5. Known gap: the paddle tail and jaws remain subtle at gameplay zoom, short of the GDD silhouette goal.

decisions.origin: creator decision: the editor opens at mating when a litter is on the way, from Generation 2; parts with no ability yet are shown locked until Phase D; committed parts work at birth where an ability already exists
decisions.decision: Phase C (EV-008 to EV-010): a draft engine (cost, validation, prerequisites, undo/redo/revert, commit), an editor controller that offers a design at a Generation 2+ mating and attaches the committed plan to the expecting mother, a reproduction bridge that shapes each newborn from that plan through the legacy anatomy axes without RNG, and an in-game editor UI (palette, preview in eight facings with walk test, site buttons with symmetry, inspector with budget, gains and losses and measured stats, keyboard, mouse and touch).
decisions.rationale: GDD Phase C gate: edit, preview, commit, reproduce, save and reload, all deterministic, with no clipped UI, large hit targets and old saves still opening. Living creatures are never edited.

implementation.notes: Gate met: headless tests/evolution-editor.mjs covers G2 offer, no retroactive edit, no RNG use, free cancel, commit spending, save/reload mid-pregnancy, deterministic litter with the design and its abilities, ancestry unlocks and part removal. Real browser: a G2 mating opens the editor; edits, locked Phase D message, test, compare, rotate, undo, redo and commit work; the litter is born with the design; in-page save and restore gives the same litter; no console errors. No clipped or overlapping UI and no button under 38 px at 1280x720, 820x600 and 390x780 (an 820 px footer overlap was found and fixed). Saves written by v1.33.7 and v1.36.0 open unchanged. Suite 152/153 before recording (provenance pending); evolution baseline matches; decision probe 5/5; 560-animal observer 16.7 ms median, p95 16.8 ms at 1x to 4x.

decisions.origin: creator decision: "just proceed, yes to all" to the Phase D plan of one ability and one cost per locked part, no new keys, and a three-body Stalker gate
decisions.decision: Phase D: part-derived abilities for digging forelimb, claw, venom gland, wide-field eye, reinforced torso and paddle tail, read only from designed body plans and folded into the existing authorities (adaptationEffects, threatSenseEffect, movementProfile, tryKill, playerStrike, playerInteract, braceResponse, predator speed). Autonomous creatures use dig and venom under the same rules. The editor unlocks all parts, swaps torsos and shows each ability and cost.
decisions.rationale: GDD Phase D gate: three clearly different body builds solve the same survival situation differently; actions cannot be triggered without parts; AI follows the same rules. Existing survival goals and progression are preserved.

implementation.notes: Gate met in the real browser (tools/phase_d_gate_probe.py, 9/9): same lean-ground Stalker charge; spring runner escapes with 0 hits; armored digger braces (0 to 9 damage against 15 for a plain body) then digs roots with E; venom and wide-eye body drives it off poisoned; wide-field eyes mark threats at 14 tiles against 10; a plain body cannot dig or poison; no console errors. tests/part-abilities.mjs covers each ability and cost, no part no action, a wild digger feeding itself, and save/reload of dug ground, poison and doses. Suite 154/155 before recording (provenance pending); v1.33.7 evolution baseline matches; decision probe 5/5; editor gate passes at 1280, 820 and 390 px. Observer probe A/B against v1.37.0 on the same machine: equal (16.7 ms median both; p95 and slow frames equally raised by machine load). During this pass an outside overwrite put v1.36.0 files over the toolkit; v1.37.0 files were restored from the staged v1.37.0 package and the Phase D edits reapplied.

decisions.rationale: Playtesters asked for deeper creature evolution; the creator set the Rule of 8 starting library and a primitive start so evolution has room to grow.

decisions.origin: creator direction
decisions.decision: Make physical build matching, not repeated mating or learned behavior, the gateway to deliberate next-generation anatomy editing. Crossbreeding compatible diverged physical builds must combine genuinely inherited parent parts and let the player stabilize a build by selective pairing. Explore part-defined egg/live/dual reproduction with explicit DNA/mass/metabolic/brood costs and breed-out tradeoffs, without claiming those modes are implemented until real incubation/hatching systems exist.
decisions.rationale: A full part-editor offer after every mating erases biological inheritance and undermines cross-lineage evolutionary divergence. Meaningful parent-mixing and deliberate stabilization allow multiple natural outcomes and consequential player-directed breeding.

implementation.notes: AI-assisted first slice: new physical crossover and matched-plan editor gating implemented. Proposed reproductive organ classes and modes are design-only.
